records.element: Script — all 8 lines (v2, locked)
records.choice: The v2 script verbatim (files/short-eo-teaser-print-script-v2.md): mystery-first structure (The Impossible Object), China/Korea credited before Gutenberg is named, the impact statistic as a mirrored beat, the message stated at L7 unannounced, the bridge after the close.
records.alternatives: v1 — scored 10/100 by Hadi and rejected; its attack list is the rewrite's spec (script doc S7).
records.context: Phase 0 study brief + Phase 1 Narrative Gate + retention records DR-1/DR-2 inside the script doc; teaser doctrine (shorts double as intros to the long-form series).
records.why: The script doc IS this section of the record; the build changes no word.
records.change: Hadi's score on the built video reopens lines through the script doc, never silently in the build.

records.element: Scene plate — the pair (L1, L7, opening card)
records.choice: Generated plate: two open Bibles on a workshop table, page rows matching, a dark wooden wall reserved above them, one candle at the edge. Inspected by eye before use (V-06): the two books genuinely read as the same book twice.
records.alternatives: A single open Bible (script DR-1's fallback if the pair failed legibility) — not needed: the pair reads at full size and at 180 px.
records.context: The script's ONE vivid detail (N-03) and its bookend object (N-08): the pair opens the piece and the close returns to it, transformed.
records.why: The hook is an object, not a topic; the frame must be holdable in the mind's eye for the whole piece.
records.change: If the 180 px cover check failed, the fallback in DR-1 governs.

records.element: Scene plate — the scribe (L2; returns at L5's second half)
records.choice: Generated plate: blank-oval monk scribe (the series figure anchor) at a sloped desk, quill in hand, candle beside a manuscript whose rows already sit unevenly. Deep shadow reserved upper-left.
records.alternatives: A close-up of the page alone — rejected: the cost in L2 is a person's three years; the person must be in the frame (the script's own weak-point 4 names the bet).
records.context: N-06: the villain (the Wandering Copy) needs its worker visible; V-03 the scene illustrates the exact words.
records.why: Drift is something a hand does; the frame shows the hand doing it.

records.element: Scene plate — clay type (L3, first half)
records.choice: Generated plate: a blank-oval craftsman in period dress placing a clay tile into a full tray of clay letter tiles, lantern light; the tile marks are blurred glyphs, not readable words (V-07). Wall reserved above.
records.alternatives: A tray without the craftsman — rejected: L3's surprise is a person four centuries early, not a museum object.
records.context: Credit order (script S1.4): China is named before Gutenberg exists in the piece.
records.why: The inversion lands as a scene, not a footnote.

records.element: Scene plate — metal type (L3, second half)
records.choice: Generated plate: a type case of grey metal sorts, tweezers beside it, one hand setting a sort. Wall reserved above.
records.alternatives: Staying on the clay plate for all of L3 — rejected: the line's turn (clay -> metal) is a change of material; the cut performs it (DR-PRINT-CUT).
records.context: S-08: a state change must construct meaning; the material change IS the sentence's second clause.
records.why: Same idea, harder material — the viewer sees the step the narration names.

records.element: Scene plate — the press (L4)
records.choice: Generated plate: the wooden screw press full-frame — handle bar, great screw, the type forme on its bed, and one freshly printed sheet beside the forme.
records.alternatives: A workshop wide shot with the press small — rejected: L4 names three parts; all three must be findable in the frame (S-04 contiguity).
records.context: L4 is the mechanism payoff (the L1 loop closes here); the parts are named in the same breath that shows them.
records.why: Metal letters, oil ink, a screw press — the frame holds all three plus the product.

records.element: Scene plate — the stacks (L5, first half)
records.choice: Generated plate: dozens of identical bound books in stacks across table and floor, calm wall reserved above.
records.alternatives: A numeral graphic ('180') drawn over the press plate — rejected: a drawn number is a claim; a room full of one book is the evidence (and code-drawn graphics fail V-13 where images can carry it).
records.context: L5 is the shareable number (script DR-2); its first half is pure count.
records.why: The arithmetic's left side is visible before it is spoken.

records.element: Scene plate — the shelves (L6)
records.choice: Generated plate: a library hall, shelves of books converging on a bright arched window; the dark stone aisle in the lower middle is the reserved word space.
records.alternatives: Reusing the stacks plate for L6 — rejected: L6 escalates from one workshop to the world; sameness would shrink the beat it must enlarge.
records.context: Payoff 3 (scale): the thousand-year reversal needs architecture, not another pile.
records.why: The reversal reads as a place you can walk into.

records.element: Scene plate — dawn finale (L8 + end card, reused)
records.choice: The series' Observations finale dawn plate, reused exactly as Ep.2/Ep.3/Ep.4 use it: empty plain at morning.
records.alternatives: A new dawn for the teaser — rejected: bookend sameness across the series is the device (series Chekhov, N-08).
records.context: The bridge (L8) frames the piece as one chapter of the planet's story; the end card rides the same world.
records.why: The print chapter joins the shelf in the same morning light as body, story, mark and song.
records.change: If the finale plate is ever rebuilt, every piece using it follows.

records.element: Scene grammar — the two mid-line plate cuts
records.choice: The plate changes INSIDE two lines, at measured silences: L3 at 22.41 s (the semicolon: clay -> metal) and L5 at 33.21 s (the mirror: stacks -> the scribe's plate). Cut times come from silencedetect pauses on the narration, not from estimates. (v3: re-measured on the v3 alignment after the stem changes — L3 pause 22.14-22.68, L5 pause 32.86-33.56.)
records.alternatives: Cuts only on line boundaries (the Ep.3 pattern) — rejected here: both lines are built as two-clause turns, and a boundary-only cut would leave the second clause illustrating the first clause's picture (V-03).
records.context: Ep.2 L7 and Ep.4 L5 established the mid-line cut; this build generalises it to a cut list in the scene config.
records.why: The picture turns exactly when the sentence turns.
records.change: If a future line's turn has no measured pause, the cut waits for the clause's first word instead.

records.element: Element layer — the stamped book (generated, deliberately NOT used)
records.choice: A glowing open book was generated on pure black for a screen-blend overlay on the press plate (the Ep.3 hand-stencil pattern) — and is NOT in the scene. Recorded as a deliberate non-use, with the asset kept in the build folder.
records.alternatives: Shipping it anyway at the least-bad seat (over the press beam) — rejected at inspection: the press plate has no designed seat for it; every candidate position overlaps the press, the type forme, the printed sheet, or the word bands.
records.context: Q-d interference + S-05 one signal at a time: the press plate already carries the system's product (the printed sheet beside the forme); a floating glowing book would double the signal and fight the focal object.
records.why: An element without a seat is decoration; decoration that competes with the mechanism fails the Qualifying Pass even when it is pretty.
records.change: If the press plate is ever regenerated with a designed alcove (an empty press bed, say), the element returns and this record is amended.

records.element: Word placement — the dark workshop scenes (pair, scribe, clay, metal, press, stacks)
records.choice: Cream words, amber key, text shadow, in each plate's reserved calm area: pair bands y 470/590 (the dark wall), scribe 320/420 (the shadow), clay 320/420 and metal 330/450 (the walls), press ONE band y 296 with the size cap (v3 — see DR-PRINT-GAP-1), stacks 320/420 (the wall).
records.alternatives: One band set for the whole piece — rejected: each plate's negative space sits elsewhere; a fixed band is the subtitle habit returning (V-16).
records.context: V-16 + V-14; placement is per-scene, planned at generation time (each plate was generated with its word space specified).
records.why: Words never cover a book, a face, a flame, or the press's working parts. In v2 one phrase ('metal letters,') grazed the top of the screw post — disclosed here in v2's record; FIXED in v3 by DR-PRINT-GAP-1 and verified on the delivered frames: no word touches the post.
records.change: Per-frame QC verdicts govern; the plan audit shows 0 V-14 violations.

records.element: Word placement — shelves + finale
records.choice: Shelves: cream/amber with shadow at y 1330/1445 — the dark stone aisle, the plate's one calm surface (bottom glyph edge 1495, inside the safe rect). Finale: brown/rust, no shadow, y 815/935 — the Ep.2/Ep.3/Ep.4 finale grammar, unchanged.
records.alternatives: Words over the shelves' bright window — rejected: the window is the plate's focal light; words there fail Q-c twice (cover + compete).
records.context: V-16 placement follows the scene; the finale's grammar is series consistency (K-02) for the shared plate.
records.why: The aisle is the walkway; the words walk it.

records.element: Word timing + chunking (all scenes)
records.choice: faster-whisper word timestamps mapped to the script's exact words (117 display words); phrases of <=3 words appear cumulatively and clear before the next phrase; key words are the script's accent set, amber at +18% with an overshoot pop. One token (L1's 'Mainz,') was started by the aligner ~0.5 s early, into the opening silence; it is clamped to the measured line onset by the house method. Seven ASR-hearing repairs are logged in words.json (down from v2's eleven; the two proper names now land as near-homophones — see DR-PRINT-GAP-2; timings kept, display words are the script's).
records.alternatives: Whole-line captions (banned) and per-word karaoke over a full line (a line on screen reads as a subtitle).
records.context: Format v4 word-animation spec; the alignment log ships in the build folder.
records.why: At most 3 words exist at any instant, each arriving with its spoken moment.
records.change: Whisper boundary error >~150 ms on a re-alignment reopens the mapping.

records.element: Music + narration track
records.choice: Guide-voice lines (the series TTS voice) normalised per line (A-11); a warm mid-register synth-pad bed — between Ep.3's low cave bed and Ep.4's high warm bed, a workshop register for the print shop (a logged variation, not a series change) — ducked ~13 dB under the voice, WITH the v3 dynamics envelope (DR-PRINT-GAP-4); stereo pan before mastering; master chain without dynaudnorm (standing law) to -13.99 LUFS / TP -1.85 on the master; music-only twin built alongside (it carries the same envelope — the dynamics belong to the music).
records.alternatives: Reusing Ep.3's or Ep.4's exact chord set — rejected: identical beds across pieces are an audio signature; the shop earns its own register.
records.context: QC A-section; A-07: the delivered file is re-measured independently in QC.
records.why: The bed's job is the workshop's warmth under the voice, never a rival to it (Q-e).
records.change: The cloned-voice pass swaps narration via the music-only twin, per the standing ladder.

records.element: Packaging — title
records.choice: "Two Identical Bibles" — the script's DR-1: the impossibility in three words, everything else withheld.
records.alternatives: 'A Book That Speaks Without Its Author' (hands over the payoff); '180 Bibles in Three Years' (a fact to file, not a mystery to open) — both rejected in the script doc.
records.context: S-09; the click is bought with an information gap.
records.why: Books used to be unique objects; sameness is the anomaly a cold viewer taps.
records.change: CTR data after publish is the comparison baseline.

records.element: Packaging — cover
records.choice: The opening-card frame (the pair + EARTH ONE + the title), the series' designated-cover practice (Ep.3/Ep.4); the script's cover line 'EXACTLY THE SAME.' stands as the packaging line in the upload package. Checked legible at 180 px in QC.
records.alternatives: A bespoke cover frame with the cover line typeset over the pair — kept as the fallback if the card frame crowds at 180 px; the QC check decides.
records.context: S-09 designated cover frame; DR-1 names the pair as the proof object.
records.why: The proof object itself, the channel, and the title — readable at feed size.
records.change: The QC 180 px verdict decides between the two named frames.

records.element: Container — opening card (1.6 s)
records.choice: Pair plate + EARTH ONE + 'TWO IDENTICAL BIBLES' in amber on the dark wall, over a soft radial scrim behind the text block (the Ep.3 fix pattern: a card-layer gradient, the artwork untouched).
records.alternatives: Cold-open on narration (the S-section's first-1.5 s promise question — a format-level question held open series-wide, not silently adopted per piece).
records.context: Earth One format v4 container; cards are titles, not subtitles — V-16 does not touch them.
records.why: The card names channel and piece before the hook — the standing container approved with Ep.1.
records.change: The open container-vs-hook question, when Hadi settles it, applies here first.

records.element: Container — end card (2.5 s)
records.choice: Finale plate + 'FOLLOW FOR THE REST OF THE STORY' + NEXT tease 'MORE OF THE PLANET'S STORY' + EARTH ONE. Duration 2.5 s per the locked script's own runtime math; the format's generic ~3.4 s end card is superseded for this piece by its locked doc, and the difference is recorded here rather than smuggled. No invented next-chapter title: the long-form print chapter is not scripted, so the tease promises the series (Ep.4's precedent — packaging may not promise what does not exist).
records.alternatives: A 3.4 s card for strict format sameness — rejected: the teaser's <=65 s ceiling and its locked runtime budget govern this piece.
records.context: Format v4 close: spoken bridge (L8) + FOLLOW end card, approved at Ep.1 i7.
records.why: The ask is made three ways — spoken bridge, card text, description — because N-09 forbids hiding it in metaphor.
records.change: When the long-form print chapter is scripted, a future iteration of this card names it.

records.element: Container — EARTH ONE bug
records.choice: Small bold 'EARTH ONE' at top-left (x=100, y=265) during content: cream at 69% on the dark workshop scenes; brown at 75% for the finale line (scene-matched ink, the Ep.4 pattern).
records.alternatives: Fixed cream everywhere — on the dawn finale it washes out; attribution that cannot be read fails its only job.
records.context: Format v4 container; V-14 safe rect (inside it, top-left).
records.why: Channel attribution that survives re-uploads and screen-record shares.

records.element: v3 fix — the press word graze (JOB TEASER-95, gap G1)
records.choice: The press line's phrases move to ONE band (cy 296) with the accent-aware size cap 86 (glyph boxes 253-339, wholly above the screw post's top at frame y ~360), AND the press plate's drift zoom is set to 0 in the scene config (plateZoom) — in v2 the zoom lifted the post top to ~322 by line end, into the band. Phrases are sequential, so one band cannot self-collide. (Margin history: the first v3 layout at cy 300 / cap 88 measured only 3 px between the 'press.' descender and the post on the delivered frame; the band and cap were tightened (cy 296, cap 86) and the delivered frame re-measured: 8 px of clean background between the descender's lowest ink and the post — the pride rule: a fix ships with margin, not at the edge.)
records.alternatives: Shifting the plate inside its frame (cover-fit is exact — no overflow to shift within); flanking phrases left/right of the post (phrase widths exceed the ~480 px flanks); regenerating the press plate (style risk, unnecessary).
records.context: Hadi scored v2 85 (2026-10-24) and ordered the improvement round; the graze was the one disclosed defect in v2's own record (DR-PRINT-WORD-1). Geometry measured on the plate file, not estimated.
records.why: A known, measured defect does not ride into the final catalogue when a layout change removes it. The press holding still reads as the machine being bolted down; every other plate keeps its drift.
records.change: If the press plate is ever regenerated with a taller clear wall, the two-band layout and the drift can return together.

records.element: v3 fix — proper-name pronunciation (JOB TEASER-95, gap G2)
records.choice: The guide voice's stems for L1, L3, L4 were regenerated with the SAME voice (avocado_v2:MAI_03) with TTS-INPUT respelling only — 'Mynts' for Mainz (L1, L4), 'Bee Shung' for Bi Sheng (L3, at speed 96). Display words stay the script's exact words. L1 is a sentence splice: its first sentence comes from the respelled take (whose full take slurred 'Two Bibles lie open'), its remainder is the shipped v2 take, joined with a 15 ms crossfade inside the measured inter-sentence pause. ASR verification: repairs fell 11 -> 7; 'Mainz' is now heard 'Mint(s)' (near-homophone of the German), 'Sheng' is now heard 'shung'.
records.alternatives: Whole-take regeneration of L1 with four different respellings — every variant slurred a previously clean phrase (the TTS is deterministic per input; changing the first word re-rolls the whole line's prosody). Keeping v2's stems — rejected: 'Minds'/'main' for Mainz teaches the wrong name in a piece whose job is teaching names.
records.context: The ASR-proxy log (words.json) is the intelligibility evidence; the recorded trade: the new L3 take swallows the possessive in 'Korea's,' (heard 'Koreas', timing kept) — a minor parse loss accepted for the name fix, and L3's pace improves 0.342 -> 0.347 s/word.
records.why: A history teaser that mispronounces its two anchors loses credibility at exactly the scholarly beats; the fix keeps every take Hadi scored except where the ear-evidence indicts it.
records.change: The voice-clone pass replaces the guide voice wholesale; these respellings retire with it.

records.element: v3 fix — the close's delivery (JOB TEASER-95, gap G3)
records.choice: L7 — the message line — was the fastest line in the piece (0.317 s/word against the 0.45 standard and the piece's own 0.37-0.44 range). Its stem is slowed with atempo 0.93 (the take Hadi scored is preserved, only its rate changes): 6.03 s -> 6.34 s of speech, 0.334 s/word; and the gap before it widens 0.55 -> 0.70 s so the chill arrives after a breath, not on L6's heels.
records.alternatives: Regenerating L7 at a lower TTS speed — rejected: a new take re-rolls the expression of the piece's most important line; atempo keeps the scored performance.
records.context: Gap analysis measured per-line pace on the v2 stems (state note in the job file); pause placement and delivery pace are inside the score-triggered gap-hunt's audit scope. The locked script's words are unchanged.
records.why: The line that should land coldest was delivered quickest; gravity is a rate, and the rate is now the piece's slowest-but-one.
records.change: Hadi's ear on v3 governs: if 0.93 reads as dragging, 0.96 is the one-parameter retreat.

records.element: v3 fix — music-bed dynamics (JOB TEASER-95, gap G4)
records.choice: The bed gains a gain envelope in build_audio.py: +2 dB swell across L5-L6 (the number and the scale), -3.5 dB dip under L7 (the close), restored for the L8 bridge; ramps >= ~1 s. In v2 the bed sat at one ducked level for all 54 s and scored the triumph and the chill identically. The voice chain is untouched (A-11 parity is a voice property; delivered parity re-measured in QC).
records.alternatives: Re-composing the bed (new chords/plucks) — rejected: the register was a logged, approved variation (DR-PRINT-MUSIC); the defect was flatness, not content.
records.context: Envelope control points are printed by the build and logged in the v3 state note; the music-only twin carries the same envelope.
records.why: A score that never moves reads as background; two shaped moves (lift, fall away) make the bed perform the piece's emotional shape without touching a note.
records.change: If the swell fights the voice in Hadi's ear, the envelope depths are single constants (SWELL/DIP) in the build.

records.element: v3 audit — the metaltype plate (JOB TEASER-95, gap G6) + the breath before the number (G5)
records.choice: Two smaller findings ride here. G5 FIXED: the gap before L5 widens 0.45 -> 0.62 s — the shareable statistic (180 Bibles) now lands after an anticipation breath instead of running straight out of the mechanism line. G6 AUDITED, PLATE KEPT: the metaltype plate is the set's plainest image (flat light, a scratched wall), but it is legible, in-style, and its word bands sit in genuinely calm space; a regeneration attempt in this round failed at the tool (input-file error, retry barred), so the plate stays and the gap is recorded rather than papered over — it is a richness gap, not a defect.
records.alternatives: Holding the whole v3 round for one plate — rejected: five verified fixes do not wait on the sixth, weakest finding.
records.context: Gap analysis ranked G6 last (MED-LOW) of six; the fix-first law binds defects, and this plate has none that QC can measure.
records.why: The record distinguishes 'fixed', 'kept by decision', and 'attempted and failed' — a 95 claim needs the full audit, not only the wins.
records.change: A future plate pass may regenerate metaltype in-style with the composition specified in the job file; the bands (330/450) remain valid for any plate with a calm upper wall.

records.element: v3 addition — word choreography (WORD CHOREOGRAPHY doctrine, Hadi 2026-10-24 ~17:43 ET; PRIDE RULE)
records.choice: Every word's animation behaviour is now a recorded decision, implemented in renderAt via each word's anim field (vocabulary: pop / stamp / drift / sink / grow / small / still). Decided behaviours: 'identical.' (L1) STAMP — the thesis word lands like a press strike; 'wander:' (L2) DRIFT — the word sways sideways as copies drift; 'years.' (L2) SINK — the three-year cost settles downward; 'metal.' (L3) STAMP — the harder material lands harder than clay; 'repeats:' and 'press.' (L4) STAMP — the mechanism striking is the line's content; '180' (L5) STAMP against 'one' (L5) SMALL — the stamped multitude against one quiet scribe's book; 'outnumbers' (L6) GROW — the word holds 1.15x, outgrowing its line; ALL of L7 (the close) STILL — fade only, no motion, matching the slowed delivery (GAP-3) and the dipped bed (GAP-4): the message stands still while everything before it moved. Every other word keeps the house pop. Behaviours affect motion only — placement, size, colour and timing are untouched. PER-WORD CONTAINER: every one of the 117 words carries its own entry in this file's word_decisions block (treatment + reason) — the choreographed words above, the close's stilled words, and every remaining word as a DELIBERATE as-is with its reason (emphasis is a budget; the record names what each quiet word is quiet FOR). Coverage: 117 of 117.
records.alternatives: Uniform pop for every word (the v2 behaviour) — rejected by the doctrine: undecided behaviour is randomness, and a close that bounces like a hook undercuts the line that must land coldest.
records.context: Doctrine: words must TELL the story, not appear and disappear; which words shrink, grow, change shape or flip is actively decided per word/beat and recorded. The choreography was added mid-build (before the render) so v3 ships it — no restart of finished parts was needed, only the scene rebuild + line re-renders.
records.why: Motion is the last free channel in a word-animation piece: when it carries meaning, the story reads sound-off; when it is uniform, it is decoration.
records.change: Hadi's re-score governs: a behaviour that distracts is removed for that word alone; the table is per-word, so no other word is affected.

accepted_exceptions_note: No accepted exception stands for this piece. The one disclosed defect of the v2 build — the 'metal letters,' phrase grazing the top of the screw post (disclosed in DR-PRINT-WORD-1) — was FIXED in the v3 build by DR-PRINT-GAP-1 and verified on the delivered frames; a fix is not an acceptance. One record-internal acceptance travels verbatim inside the records: DR-PRINT-GAP-2 (the v3 proper-name pronunciation fix) records that the new L3 take swallows the possessive in 'Korea's,' (heard 'Koreas', timing kept) — a minor parse loss accepted for the name fix, inside the scene's own decision text.
